_contract: World-bible timeline. Acts follow GDD §12.3 (I: D1-3, II: D4-8, III: D9-11). reveal = when the PLAYER learns it: {district, min_stage} via DistrictData.Stage; era = when it HAPPENED. refs point at character/faction/note ids only.

events.text_en: The city grid goes up district by district; one lamplighter signs on and stays forty years, logging every lamp by hand (14,207 orders before the blackout).
A research program taps the grid 'to store what the lamps have seen'. Officially denied, repeatedly. Its test feeders run at night; three apartment meters later spin backwards.
Residents report the park trees 'lean toward the lamps to listen'. The parks office closes the park and denies it. The closure notice is stamped weeks before the lights fail.
Rolling outage scheduled 22:00-23:00 never ends. The feeder draw doesn't add up; the substation transformer is warm while dark. The city goes to silhouettes; the first watch rosters form.
Leaflets order orderly evacuation to the central arena, one bag per person, no outdoors after dark. The issuing office and date are torn off every copy; nobody who went is mentioned again.
The grid crew proves a single streetlight can burn off scavenged parts. The proof becomes the game's loop and the crew's creed: darkness is reversible, district by district.
The crew finds the suburban draw's source: a transformer warm after two weeks dark. They log it, cache proof at the bench, and decide to walk to the substation.
Crossing the park, the crew loses Petrov to something that hunts running sound and carries him 'toward the water'. Survivors leave the cache at the keeper's shed and the warning: walk, always walk.

The Keeper begins dismantling lit-capable lamps citywide ('every lamp I take apart is a lamp they cannot drink'), sending transformers toward the center. Work order 14,208 is the first; the manifesto follows.

A calm voice begins looping on shortwave: restore the grid district by district, go to the power station, 'the one who kept the light will meet you at the light.' The player's Act I directive (GDD §12.3).

A grid engineer with a flashlight enters the suburbs. Eleven districts dark, one bench-proven truth, and a city that remembers being lit. The player is the first person moving toward the center since the crew.
